examples.ko: 엄마가 우는 아이를 두 팔로 감싸안았어요.
examples.en: The mother held her crying child in both arms.

examples.ko: 그는 아픈 친구의 어깨를 감싸안고 위로했어요.
examples.en: He put his arm around his sick friend's shoulders and comforted him.

examples.ko: 추워서 무릎을 감싸안은 채 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I sat hugging my knees.
It feels like the warm sunlight is embracing the village.

examples.ko: 실수한 후배를 감싸안아 주는 선배가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a senior who stands by a junior who made a mistake.

examples.ko: 서로의 다름을 감싸안을 수 있는 사회가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like a society that can embrace each other's differences.

explain: 그냥 '안다'보다 팔로 둘러 포근하게 안는 느낌이에요. 사람의 허물이나 다름을 너그럽게 받아들인다는 비유로도 써요. '감싸다'는 보호하거나 덮어 가린다는 쪽이라 조금 달라요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '안다', it feels like wrapping your arms around someone warmly. It is also used figuratively for generously accepting someone's faults or differences. '감싸다' leans toward protecting or covering something, so it is a little different.

examples.en: The child seems sleepy and keeps blinking.

examples.ko: 소가 큰 눈을 끔벅거리며 서 있어요.
examples.en: The cow stands there slowly blinking its big eyes.
The sunlight was dazzling, so I kept blinking.

examples.ko: 눈을 끔벅거리는 걸 보니 졸린가 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you blinking, you must be sleepy.
Grandfather just kept blinking without saying a word.
I was blinking sleepily and ended up falling asleep.

explain: '깜박이다'보다 느릿하고 둔하게 눈을 감았다 떠요. 졸리거나 멍할 때, 소처럼 눈이 큰 동물에게 잘 어울려요. '끔벅대다'도 같은 느낌으로 써요.
explain_en: It means opening and closing the eyes, but feels slower and duller than '깜박이다'. It suits moments of sleepiness or daze, and animals with big eyes. '끔벅대다' is a similar word.

examples.en: The laundry hung on the roof flutters in the wind.
His hair fluttered every time he ran.
I took photos in a flowing skirt.
The big shirt flaps around, so it's a bit uncomfortable.
The Korean flag is waving in front of the school.

examples.ko: 너풀거릴 정도로 큰 옷은 사지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't buy clothes so big that they flap around.

explain: 천이나 머리카락처럼 얇고 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 흔들릴 때 써요. 헐렁한 옷이 몸 주위에서 흔들리는 모습에도 잘 어울려요. '너울거리다'는 더 느리고 크게 물결치는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when something thin and light, like cloth or hair, keeps moving in the wind. It also fits loose clothes flapping around the body. '너울거리다' feels slower and more wavelike.

examples.en: The players struggled hard to the end but sadly lost.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 가족을 위해 열심히 분투해요.
examples.en: He struggles hard for his family.

examples.ko: 작은 가게를 지키려고 분투하는 사장님이 계세요.
examples.en: There is an owner who is fighting hard to keep a small shop.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 우승을 위해 분투하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is striving hard to win the championship.
The story of struggling in a hard environment is moving.
Don't struggle alone; ask for help.

explain: 어려운 조건에서 힘을 다해 애쓰는 모습에 써요. 결과보다 노력하는 과정을 인정하는 느낌이라 스포츠 중계나 기사에 자주 나와요. '고군분투하다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Use it for putting in all your strength under hard conditions. It recognizes the effort more than the result, so it often appears in sports commentary and articles. People also say '고군분투하다'.

examples.en: The kids were playing with fire and almost started a big blaze.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 불장난하다 혼난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I got scolded for playing with fire.

examples.ko: 건조한 날에는 산 근처에서 불장난하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: On dry days, you must not play with fire near the mountains.

examples.ko: 동생이 라이터로 불장난하는 걸 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled to see my younger sibling playing with a lighter.

examples.ko: 그런 위험한 일은 불장난하듯 가볍게 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat a dangerous thing like that as lightly as a game with fire.
If you treat romance like a game with fire, both people get hurt.

explain: 말 그대로 불을 가지고 노는 것인데, 비유로 가벼운 마음으로 위험한 일이나 연애를 하는 것에도 써요. 어른이 아이를 혼낼 때 '불장난하면 안 돼'라고 많이 말해요. 비유로 쓸 때는 책임지지 않는 가벼운 태도를 비판하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: That wasn't love, it was just a fling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 마음 없이 가볍게 시작한 위험한 관계나 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A risky relationship or act begun casually, without real commitment.

explain_en: It literally means playing with fire, and figuratively it covers doing something risky or having a romance with a careless attitude. Adults often scold children with '불장난하면 안 돼'. Used figuratively, it criticizes an irresponsible, casual attitude.

examples.en: The door creaks in the wind.
The old chair creaked every time I sat down.
The floor creaked, so I walked carefully.
The sound of the bed creaking woke me up.
The stairs creak, so please come down slowly.
The old bicycle creaked as it went up the hill.

explain: 문이나 마루, 의자 같은 것이 소리를 반복해서 내는 모습이에요. 소리가 한 번 날 때는 '삐거덕 소리가 나다'라고 해요. 같은 뜻으로 '삐걱거리다'도 써요.
explain_en: It describes things like doors, floors and chairs making that creaking sound repeatedly. For a single creak you say '삐거덕 소리가 나다'. '삐걱거리다' is also used with the same meaning.

en: desperate struggle; life-or-death struggle; battle for survival

examples.ko: 구조대는 밤새 폭우 속에서 사투를 벌였어요.
examples.en: The rescue team fought a desperate struggle in the heavy rain all night.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 끝없는 사투 끝에 결국 우승했어요.
examples.en: After an endless struggle, that player finally won the championship.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나는 건 저에게 매일이 사투였어요.
examples.en: For me, getting up in the morning was a battle every day.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 생존을 건 사투가 이어졌어요.
examples.en: A fight for survival went on at the top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 그는 병과의 사투에서 끝내 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: He finally won his fight against the illness.

examples.ko: 오랜 사투로 얻은 합격이라 더 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm even happier because I earned this pass through a long struggle.

explain: 주로 '사투를 벌이다' 꼴로 쓰고, 목숨을 걸 만큼 필사적인 싸움이에요. 일상에서는 '졸음과의 사투'처럼 조금 과장해서 말하기도 해요. 방언을 뜻하는 '사투리'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '사투를 벌이다', a fight so desperate it is as if life were at stake. In daily talk people exaggerate a bit, as in '졸음과의 사투' (a battle against sleepiness). It is a different word from '사투리' (dialect), so don't mix them up.

examples.en: He left without saying a single word.
Let alone an apology, there wasn't even a word of explanation.
Couldn't you have at least said a word beforehand?

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 일언반구조차 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't say so much as a word about that matter.
My friend didn't answer with even a word, so I felt hurt.

examples.ko: 회사에서 일언반구 통보도 없이 계약을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The company ended the contract without any notice at all.

explain: 거의 항상 '없다, 않다' 같은 부정의 말과 함께 써서 '한마디도 없이'라는 섭섭함이나 불만을 나타내요. '일언반구도 없이', '일언반구 말이 없다'처럼 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '한마디도'라고 해요.
explain_en: It almost always goes with a negative such as '없다' or '않다', expressing disappointment or complaint that there was not even one word. It appears as '일언반구도 없이' or '일언반구 말이 없다'. In everyday talk people say '한마디도'.
